name: GA-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+15 partisan lean strongly favors the incumbent party
Brian Jack has a massive fundraising edge ($2.0M vs $0.15M) and $1.1M cash on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at only about 4%
First-term incumbent with no notable opposition activity or outside spending against him
model.rationale: The district's R+15 lean, Jack's incumbency and overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing Democratic odds near 4% all point the same direction, with no polls or ratings suggesting any complication. The forecast sits slightly beyond the fundamentals-based estimate to reflect the incumbent's dominance of the money race.
model.watch: Any emergence of outside spending against Jack or a shift in the national environment toward Democrats would be the first sign this is closer than expected.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 3rd District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of R+15, and first-term Republican Brian Jack is running for reelection after clearing his primary. Democrat Maura Keller faces a steep structural disadvantage in a district that favored Republicans by a wide margin at the presidential level.

The resource gap is stark: Jack has raised about $2.0 million and holds $1.1 million on hand, while Keller has raised roughly $150,000 with under $90,000 available. No independent spending has been reported on either side, and prediction markets give Keller only about a 4% chance of winning. Absent unexpected developments, Jack is strongly favored to hold the seat.
